title: The properties panel fits on the screen it has
goal: Pick two text layers and the properties panel down the right hand side is taller than the tallest window a laptop screen allows, so Corner Radius and the rest of the Effects section are always below the fold. Anyone rounding the corners of what they picked has to scroll and hunt for the control every single time.
notes: Found on 2026-09-07 while making mixed-one-look-walk honest. Measured, not guessed: the walk asks for a 1180pt window and this display gives it 1028pt of content; the dock reports dockViewport 996 against sections running Layers 6-217, Text 217-393, Position & Size 393-528, Appearance 528-858, Effects 858-1016 with ONE layer picked, and a second layer adds an Arrange section that pushes the total to roughly 1310. Corner Radius is the last row of the last section, so it sits about 290pt below the fold. Reproduce with Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/mixed-one-look-walk.json and read panel-two-picked.json in the out folder: every Effects control comes back inWindow=false. Worth an adversarial look before building: collapsing sections by default, moving Corner Radius up next to the other shape controls, and letting the dock use two columns are all different products, and the mocks do not settle it.
acceptance: With two text layers picked in a window as tall as the screen allows, Corner Radius can be used without scrolling the panel
Nothing that was reachable before the change becomes harder to reach
It holds for one picked layer and for three or more, not just for two
